name: נַחְשׁוֹן
summary: Nahshon son of Amminadab, prince of Judah in the wilderness: his sister Elisheba was Aaron’s wife; he led Judah’s camp, which camped on the east and set out first (Num 2:3; 10:14), and brought the first offering at the dedication of the altar (Num 7:12). He is in the line from Judah to David through Salmon and Boaz (Rut 4:20; 1Ch 2:10–11), and so in the genealogies of Jesus (Mat 1:4; Luk 3:32). The name is נָחָשׁ “serpent” with the ending ‑ôn, as שִׁמְשׁוֹן Samson is שֶׁמֶשׁ “sun” with it: “of the serpent, serpent-like”, or “little serpent”. A link to נְחֹשֶׁת “bronze” cannot be ruled out, but the spelling follows נָחָשׁ.

evidence.note: “The standard of the camp of the children of Judah set out first … and over its host was נַחְשׁוֹן בֶּן־עַמִּינָדָב.”
Aaron took Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, “the sister of נַחְשׁוֹן”.
The man of Judah to stand with Moses at the numbering.
“The prince of the children of Judah, נַחְשׁוֹן בֶּן־עַמִּינָדָב”, camping toward the sunrise.
“He who offered his offering on the first day was נַחְשׁוֹן.”
“Amminadab begot נַחְשׁוֹן, and נַחְשׁוֹן begot Salmah.”
“Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah”, who begot Salma, who begot Boaz.
Ναασσών in the genealogy of Jesus Christ.
The word the name is formed from: הַנָּחָשׁ, the serpent.
שִׁמְשׁוֹן, the same pattern of noun with ‑ôn.

note: The ‑ôn ending is read as adjectival or diminutive from the pattern of names like שִׁמְשׁוֹן; scripture gives no explanation of the name. The Septuagint and New Testament spell it Ναασσών.
